You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Unannounced UI Changes Disrupt Workflow",
 "problem_statement": "Staff are confused and forced to relearn the system after unexpected interface changes, leading to errors, delays, and wasted training time. Without advance notice or previews, these disruptions hurt accuracy and efficiency in claims and payments processing."
}

 {

 },
 {

 },
 {
  "id": "573ca417ce82f613",

 }
]

<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word from one insight cited in the same sentence.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

Your previous draft failed these checks. Fix them and write the brief again.
- uncited_claims: no citation: Specific accounts have reported significant operational impact.
- quotes: quoted text is not the quote of a cited insight: we had to retrain three people just to find the new location
- quotes: quoted text is not the quote of a cited insight: hurting our efficiency
- numbers: 'Three accounts' does not match the fact sheet ([7])
</failed_checks>
<previous_draft>
## Problem
Staff are confused and forced to relearn the system after unexpected interface changes, leading to errors, delays, and wasted training time. Without advance notice or previews, these disruptions hurt accuracy and efficiency in claims and payments processing.

## Who is affected
- **Account Management teams** at multiple customer firms report that unannounced changes force retraining and cause errors in claims and payments processing [i:27a70a943d3863cd][i:695ce5df664b4bfc][i:86e3ed2f99935808].
- **Support teams** across accounts cite the need to retrain staff mid-cycle due to unexpected changes, which disrupts operations and causes processing errors [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f][i:573ca417ce82f613][i:9c432aa4bd712320].
- **Sales teams** in conversations with customers hear that interface changes are throwing off team rhythm and causing delays, with a request for more warning [i:0b22ff2ce3aa3793][i:211006eeabec013f][i:5ed8a4c145f561c2].
- **Onboarding** feedback indicates a need for advance notice and previews of changes to prevent confusion and delays [i:1510a29a4fb29690].

## Evidence
- The issue has been raised by **7** accounts across **4** routes, with a total of **17** mentions [i:0b22ff2ce3aa3793][i:1510a29a4fb29690][i:211006eeabec013f].
- The total Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) of the cited accounts is **7360000.0** GBP [i:27a70a943d3863cd][i:3a4ae29f32b5253f][i:3c7de4adbd5cede1].
- Specific accounts have reported significant operational impact. For example, Linnet House Insurance (ARR **360000.0** GBP) stated, "we had to retrain three people just to find the new location, and someone even submitted a payment in error because the button moved" [i:71a03e5a571c2a63]. Callowfield Auto Assurance (ARR **1250000.0** GBP) reported that unannounced screen changes are "hurting our efficiency" [i:695ce5df664b4bfc]. Quillon Business Insurance (ARR **860000.0** GBP) said, "We’ve had to retrain our claims team twice in three months because of unannounced screen changes — it’s disruptive and costly" [i:cf4fe8c6ca8d873d].
- Three accounts have renewals in the next 90 days: Stannary Commercial renews on **2026-12-05** [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f], Hollinbrook Home Insurance renews on **2027-01-15** [i:86e3ed2f99935808], and Quillon Business Insurance renews on **2027-01-20** [i:27a70a943d3863cd].

## Why now
- Feedback has been consistently reported across the **sales**, **onboarding**, **account_management**, and **support** routes over the last two months, with multiple mentions in **September** and **October 2026** [i:27a70a943d3863cd][i:3a4ae29f32b5253f][i:5ed8a4c145f561c2].
- The issue directly impacts core claims-handling workflows, such as processing reserves and payments, where errors have immediate financial consequences [i:27a70a943d3863cd][i:71a03e5a571c2a63].
- With **3** renewals occurring within the next 90 days, the operational disruption and associated costs are a current and pressing concern for these customers [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f][i:86e3ed2f99935808][i:cf4fe8c6ca8d873d].
</previous_draft>
